 El Nino continues to maintain very strong intensity - heavy rains concentrated in central Vietnam.
 Regarding total rainfall in the months, in Northern Vietnam, December had a total rainfall 5-15mm higher than the multi-year average, while the area from Thanh Hoa to northern Quang Tri generally had rainfall close to the multi-year average.
 VietnamPlus • 16/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 According to the National Center for Meteorological and Hydrological Forecasting, from December 2026 to February 2027, the El Nino phenomenon will continue to maintain a very strong intensity with a high probability of 79%.
 Heavy rains are occurring in Central Vietnam.
 Regarding weather patterns from December 2026 to February 2027, the National Center for Hydro-Meteorological Forecasting stated that in December, the Central region still has the possibility of moderate to heavy rain, concentrated in the area from Ha Tinh to Hue city and the South Central Coast.
 However, it should be noted that there is a possibility of a shortfall in total rainfall compared to the multi-year average in many areas of Central Vietnam even during the rainy season. Moderate to heavy rainfall is expected to decrease in January 2027.
 Regarding total rainfall in the months, in Northern Vietnam, December had a total rainfall 5-15mm higher than the multi-year average, while the area from Thanh Hoa to northern Quang Tri generally had rainfall close to the multi-year average.
 From southern Quang Tri to Hue city, rainfall is generally lower than the multi-year average by 20-40mm.
 The South Central Coast received 50-150mm less rainfall than the multi-year average. The Central Highlands and Southern Vietnam experienced 10-20mm less rainfall than the multi-year average for the same period.
 In January 2027, rainfall in Northern Vietnam and the area from Thanh Hoa to Ha Tinh will generally be close to the multi-year average; other areas will experience 10-30mm less rainfall than the multi-year average; the Central Highlands and Southern Vietnam will experience little rain. In February, rainfall in Northern Vietnam is likely to be close to the multi-year average; Central Vietnam will experience 10-20mm less rainfall than the multi-year average; the Central Highlands and Southern Vietnam will experience little rain.
 In the Mekong River basin, total rainfall in the upper reaches during December is generally 10-20% higher than the multi-year average for the same period. January and February 2027 are expected to be dry.
 In the middle reaches of the region, rainfall from December 2026 to January 2027 will generally be 10-30% lower than the multi-year average; however, in the northern part of the region, rainfall in December 2026 will be approximately the same as the multi-year average for the same period. February will generally see little rain.
 In the downstream area, rainfall in December 2026 will generally be 20-40% lower than the multi-year average. In January 2027, it will be 30-60% lower than the multi-year average for the same period. February will generally have little rain.
 The average temperature trend across the country from December 2026 to February 2027 is expected to be 1-2 degrees Celsius higher than the multi-year average for the same period. In the Southeast region, hot weather is likely to appear from February 2027, earlier than the multi-year average.
 Cold air masses are likely to be weaker than the multi-year average. Severe cold spells are likely to occur later than usual; the number of days with severe cold spells in Northern Vietnam and North Central Vietnam will generally be lower than the multi-year average for the same period. However, there is still a possibility of short-lived periods of severe cold spells causing sharp temperature drops.
 "From December 2026 to February 2027, the number of storms and tropical depressions active in the East Sea region is likely to be lower than the multi-year average, with little chance of making landfall (the multi-year average in the East Sea is 1.4 storms; making landfall is 0.2 storms). Across the country, there is a possibility of dangerous weather phenomena such as thunderstorms, tornadoes, lightning, hail, and strong gusts of wind," noted Nguyen Duc Hoa, Deputy Head of the Climate Forecasting Department.
 You may also like From March to May 2027, hot weather is expected to intensify.
 The National Center for Hydro-Meteorological Forecasting predicts that from March to May, the average temperature nationwide will generally be 1-2 degrees Celsius higher than the multi-year average for the same period, with some areas exceeding 2 degrees Celsius. From March onwards, hot weather tends to intensify in the Central Highlands and Southern Vietnam.
 In the Northwest and North Central regions, localized heatwaves are likely to occur from March. In April and May, heatwaves tend to intensify and spread across the Northern and Central regions.
 During this period, the El Niño phenomenon is likely to continue with a probability of about 80%, although its intensity tends to weaken significantly.
 Of these, weak to moderate El Nino is predominant with a probability of about 78%, strong El Nino accounts for only about 2%; the probability of transitioning to a neutral ENSO state is about 20%.
 Regarding the total rainfall during the forecast period, the National Center for Hydro-Meteorological Forecasting reported that in March, rainfall in the North and Central regions was 10-20mm lower than the multi-year average, while the Central Highlands and Southern regions generally experienced little rain.
 In April, rainfall in Northern Vietnam is likely to be 10-20mm lower than the multi-year average; Central and Southern Vietnam tend to have rainfall 20-40mm lower than the multi-year average.
 In May, rainfall was generally 10-35% lower than the multi-year average for the same period, except in the northeastern mountainous region where total rainfall was approximately the same as the multi-year average for the same period. 
 Specifically, rainfall in the Northern region in March is generally 20-50mm, with some areas receiving more. In April, it is generally 40-100mm, with some areas receiving more. In May, it is generally 140-190mm, with some areas receiving even more.
 In the Central region, rainfall in March is commonly 30-60mm. In April, it is commonly 40-70mm. In May, it is commonly 70-150mm.
 In the Central Highlands and Southern regions, March generally sees little rainfall (10-20mm/month). April typically receives 40-80mm, with some areas receiving even less. May generally receives 110-190mm, with some areas receiving even less. The rainy season in this region is likely to arrive later than the average for the same period in previous years.
 In March, the Mekong River basin experienced a 15-30% deficit in total rainfall in the upper and middle reaches compared to the multi-year average, while the lower reaches experienced a 20-50% deficit compared to the multi-year average.
 In April, the basin experienced a widespread deficit of 20-50% compared to the multi-year average. In May, the basin experienced a widespread deficit of 15-30% compared to the multi-year average.
 Deputy Head of the Climate Forecasting Department Nguyen Duc Hoa emphasized that from March to May, there is little chance of typhoons or tropical depressions appearing in the East Sea region (the average over many years in the East Sea is 0.8 storms; making landfall is 0 storms).
 You may also like Cold air masses tend to be less active than the multi-year average. During the late winter period, the number of days with light rain or drizzle in the North is likely to be less than the multi-year average.
 Additionally, showers and thunderstorms are possible in the Northern and North Central regions, with localized moderate to heavy rainfall. From May onwards, thunderstorms will increase in the Central Highlands and Southern regions, and will continue to occur in the Northern and North Central regions. During thunderstorms, be wary of tornadoes, lightning, hail, and strong gusts of wind.
 Meteorological and hydrological experts warn that the activity of the Northeast monsoon could cause strong winds and large waves in the East Sea, affecting maritime activities and fishing.
 In addition, heavy rains , thunderstorms, tornadoes, lightning, hail, and severe cold weather can adversely affect production activities, public health, crops, and livestock. From around May, the Southwest monsoon is likely to become active and cause strong winds in the southern sea areas. 
 Furthermore, during the period from March to May, the Central Highlands and Southern regions are likely to experience rainfall shortages, combined with high temperatures and the possibility of a late rainy season, increasing the risk of drought and water scarcity for daily life and production, affecting agricultural production and people's livelihoods.
 In the context of climate change, weather and climate patterns are becoming increasingly complex, with many dangerous and extreme forms such as heatwaves, heavy rainfall in short periods, flash floods, landslides, etc.
 Therefore, the meteorological and hydrological agency recommends regularly updating and integrating meteorological and hydrological forecast and warning information into short-term bulletins (1-3 days) to promptly adjust production plans and response measures, especially reservoir operation plans, ensuring the safety of the structures and downstream areas, as well as ensuring the safety of production activities and people's lives.
